Subject: Runtime channel encryption and rotation QnA — HarborBank RFI

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for taking our RFI. A few items jumped out while we reviewed the security architecture materials — we want to make sure we understand Redwood's posture for live inference channels and certificate lifecycle. Specifically:

1) How do you encrypt and authenticate inter-service channels between inference workers, sidecars, and the control plane? Are mTLS and per-session keys enforced end-to-end?
2) How are TLS certificates provisioned and rotated for runtime components? Do you support short-lived certs (<=24h) and automated rotation without service restarts?
3) In failover scenarios (zone loss / control-plane unavailability), what guarantees exist around preserving confidentiality for in-flight requests and persisted caches?
4) Can you provide a simple network/dataflow diagram that highlights the encryption domains and where material keys live?

Can you reply with concise answers and an annotated diagram? We’ll include the response in our evidence packet for the procurement review.

Best,

Laura Chen
Senior Manager, Cloud Security
HarborBank

Subject: Re: Runtime channel encryption and rotation QnA — HarborBank RFI

Hi Laura,

Thanks — quick answers below and attached is an annotated diagram (runtime-channel-diagram-v2.png). We can expand any section you want into a short evidence packet.

1) Inter-service encryption and authentication
- All service-to-service traffic inside the Redwood runtime is authenticated with mutual TLS (mTLS) using per-instance identities. We run a service mesh overlay for control-plane orchestrated routing; sidecars terminate mTLS locally so application containers never see plaintext network traffic.
- For GPU inference workers and KV/cache proxies, we additionally enable application-layer signing for critical control messages (checksum + HMAC) to defend against tampering in mixed-tenant environments.

2) Certificate provisioning and rotation
- Certificates are issued by our internal PKI and backed by customer-specific short-lived leaf certs when requested. Default rotation cadence is 24 hours for runtime leaf certs; intermediate and root certificates follow a longer lifecycle and are maintained by our security ops.
- Rotation is automated via our certificate manager (built on ACME-like automation + integration to KMS/HSM for private key protection). Rotations are handled as hot-reload operations at the sidecar/kernel layer — no full service restart required.

3) Failover and in-flight confidentiality guarantees
- In-flight encryption: because end-to-end encryption is enforced between client egress and worker ingress, in-flight payloads remain encrypted across network hops. Ephemeral session keys are negotiated per request window and discarded after completion.
- Cache persistence: cached KV blobs are encrypted at rest with envelope encryption and a tenant-specific key. During zone failover we replicate encrypted blobs; decryption keys are only available within the target zone after operator-approved key rehydration. This ensures cached content remains opaque to intermediate routing components.

4) Diagram notes (attached)
- The diagram highlights three encryption domains: client-egress, intra-runtime (sidecar <-> worker), and control-plane. The PKI root and HSM boundaries are shown; material private keys never leave the HSM-backed KMS.

Attachments: runtime-channel-diagram-v2.png (annotated), harborbank-evidence-packet.pdf (summary + proof points).

If useful, Kimberly can add a short threat-model appendix with attacker paths and mitigations. Shall we schedule a 30-min follow-up to walk through the diagram?

Best,

Hi Laura — quick follow-up from security architecture: 

- Tenant certs issuance: We support both modes. By default certs are generated per-tenant at onboarding and are short-lived (24h) with automatic refresh. For higher assurance customers we can issue ephemeral per-session leaf certs on-demand (session-bound, <1h TTL). All issuance and rotation events are logged to our audit stream (immutable append-only ledger) and are exportable to your SIEM via secure pull or push; entries include cert serial, issuer, subject, requesting principal, and timestamp.

- Cache rehydration: Rehydration is policy-driven. Default enterprise setting requires an operator-approved key rehydration step (two-person approval) for cross-zone unseal. We can provide an alternative automated rehydration flow for customers that require rapid failover; that flow is gatekept by a cryptographic attestation and recorded in the audit trail.

Drive link with diagrams and a short threat appendix: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-runtime-channel-evidence
